Activity 1: Who is John Doe?

Investigating Digital Footprints

Unit 2 Export to PDF Open dossier
Step 1

Open the John Doe Dossier

You will explore a set of images from a fictional person called John Doe. All of these images were found publicly online.

  • Open the dossier and scan all 15 evidence images.
  • For each image, ask: “What does this reveal about John?”
Open dossier
Step 2

Set Up Your Investigation Table

Create this table in your exercise book (one row per evidence image):

Image number What does this image reveal? Public or private? Why?
(e.g. 1)

Fill in the table as you look at the images. Choose any details you spot, big or small.

Step 3

Find 10+ Clues

Using the evidence images, find at least 10 pieces of information about John.

Your list must include:

  • John’s name
  • John’s date of birth (day + month)
  • The city John lives in

After that, add any other clues you can reasonably work out (hobbies, routine, places he visits, things he likes, family information, etc.).

Step 4

Decide: Public or Private?

In the last column of your table, explain whether each clue should be public or private.

  • Could this help someone identify or locate John?
  • Could this harm John’s reputation or safety?
  • Is it “nice to share” or “risky to share”?
Step 5

Reflection

A. What picture can you build of John Doe?

Write 4–5 bullet points describing what kind of person John appears to be based only on the information you found.

B. What should have stayed private?

Choose three items from your table that you think should not have been shared publicly. For each one, write one sentence explaining the risk or concern.

Step 6

Partner Discussion

Discuss your findings with the person next to you. Share one thing you discovered that you didn’t expect.

By the end of this task, you should be able to…

  • Explain the difference between public and private information online
  • Recognise how small pieces of data can build a picture of someone
  • Understand why sharing too much online can be risky
  • Describe what responsible digital behaviour looks like
